newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Privatisation seen key to Botswana economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Privatisation seen key to Botswana economic growth.

text.p: The Botswana government needs to speed up its privatisation process if it wants the private sector to be the driving force behind further economic development, an international fund manager said on Thursday.

"Unless you give the private sector, the opportunity to manage large entities like the telephone company...it will never develop as the economic driving force," said Mark Mobius, emerging markets division head at Templeton Asset Management.
He told Reuters in a telephone interview that capital flows into Botswana were being inhibited by market illiquidity and an absence of investment targets.
"Botswana is not at the top of our list because the market is not liquid enough. It is very cheap, but there are not enough places to put our money," Mobius said.

In its 1995 annual report, the Botswana Development Corporation (BDC) said it was to privatise 41 of its 114 parastatal enterprises within five years. BDC has so far divested from eight and is negotiating another seven.
Botswana Telecommunications recently announced it was moving towards privatisation, although it gave no timetable.
Mobius said the current low level of productivity was the result of a lack of incentives for workers and was tied to the government's failure to push privatisation.
"You have a situation where the government is such a big part of the economy that low productivity becomes endemic."
But Mobius noted Botswana's 30-year-old multi-party democracy and record of non-violent change were factors that were encouraging to foreign investors.
"Investors like at least a two party system, where there can be peaceful transition from one group to another," Mobius said.
